artifacts.notes:
WHAT THIS IS: uncorrected optical character recognition of a whole Ambrosian
Missal of 1499, 56,062 LF-terminated lines, valid UTF-8, no CR bytes, no form
feeds, no NUL bytes, ending in a newline. It is registered as a source artifact
and nothing more, and it is deliberately NOT structured as liturgical records.
THERE ARE NO PAGE BOUNDARIES IN THIS FILE, so a line range over it is not a
printed-page range; addressability by identity belongs to passage records with
real loci over these exact bytes.

OCR QUALITY, AND IT IS THE WORST FILE THIS LANE ACQUIRED. Measured here by
scripts/_ocr_quality.py at a Latin function-word share of 0.0537 over 185,461
tokens, English 0.0202, classified `degraded-latin` -- below the 0.0788 of the
1570 blackletter Roman missal and far below the roughly ten per cent at which
that tool says running Latin prose sits. The cause is the type. This is an
incunable set in a heavily abbreviated gothic face with long s, Tironian et and
scribal suspensions, and the recognition collapses it: `oomine` for Domine,
`0ancri` for Sancti, `pcedcrc` for procedere, `co: nouu:` for cor novum. Whole
ornamental initials are emitted as line noise or not at all.

DO NOT REST A NEGATIVE SEARCH ON THIS ARTIFACT. THIS IS NOT A FORM OF WORDS. A
thirty-two-probe anachronism battery over this file and over its per-leaf
recognition returned THIRTY-TWO NEGATIVES, and not one of them is admitted as
evidence about the book: at this level of damage an absent string is a fact about
the recognition. The edition's date rests on the colophon read in the page image,
which is the only reading in this whole acquisition that the text layer could not
supply. It is admitted `indexable` so that later passages can pin physical line
ranges over it, not so that a search over it can be reported as a finding.

A TRAP THAT WAS WALKED INTO AND IS WRITTEN DOWN SO NOBODY REPEATS IT. Line 970
reads `0ancri marroli arcbiepifcopi mediolani` and was first taken for Sancti
CAROLI archiepiscopi Mediolani -- St Charles Borromeo, canonized 1610, in a 1499
book, which would have been decisive. It is St MAROLUS, archbishop of Milan, died
423, whose feast is 23 April and who stands in the Ambrosian kalendar where a
Roman book has nobody. The neighbouring kalendar entries are of the same kind:
`Sancti Castriciani archiepiscopi Mediolani` at line 2550, Castritian being the
first bishop of Milan. AN AMBROSIAN KALENDAR IS FULL OF MILANESE ARCHBISHOP-SAINTS
AND MOST OF THEM ARE LATE ANTIQUE. A reader sweeping this rite for anachronisms
must expect that and read the whole line before believing a hit.

WHAT THE FILE CONTAINS AND WHERE, READ RATHER THAN ASSUMED. The kalendar runs
from about line 640 to about line 2600, with the Milanese sanctoral in it. The
temporal and the Masses follow. The Requiem Masses and the Masses for the dead
run from about line 20000. The blessings -- `Benedictio ad quaecunque indumenta
sacris usibus utenda`, `Benedictio stolae`, `Benedictio incensi`, `Benedictio
panis` -- close the book on leaf n384 and are the last thing before the colophon.
The file ends where the book ends and not where the scan was cut short.

IDENTITY AND EXTENT. Internet Archive item `OEXV698`, 394 leaves, `imagecount =
394`, matching the 394 `<OBJECT>` elements of the item's own djvu.xml counted
here. The companion page-image container is the item's `OEXV698.pdf`,
1,203,559,890 bytes, which is NOT registered: at 1.2 GB it is far beyond what
this repository has cause to hold, and nothing in this record depends on it
except the colophon, which was read from the item's per-leaf image derivative.
The copy is Bibliotheque Sainte-Genevieve OEXV 698 RES, catalogued as wanting
leaves [*]1 and m8, Sudoc notice 10011993X. Uploaded 2012-04-06.

WHAT A READER MUST DO BEFORE READING ANY LITURGY OUT OF THIS BOOK. Nothing in
this repository has read a unit of the Ambrosian use, and this artifact does not
make it readable: `read_from = "not-read"` on the witness row in
src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml is still correct and was not
touched by the lane that wrote this record. Given the OCR, the next lane will
need the page images for anything it means to quote.
artifacts.rights_basis:
Public domain in the United States because the book was first published outside
the United States before the pre-1931 line, and on that ground alone.

THE LINE, AND THE YEAR IT WAS DERIVED FOR. Any work first published abroad before
1931 is out of United States copyright; that is the line guidance/missals.md
records from Cornell's public-domain chart as current on 1 January 2026. THE LINE
MOVES EVERY JANUARY, which guidance/missals.md:249 states in terms, so it is
written here as DERIVED FOR CALENDAR YEAR 2026 and not as a standing rule: on
1 January 2027 it becomes before 1932, and a later reader must re-derive it
rather than quote this sentence. Publication on 27 August 1499 clears the 2026
line by four hundred and thirty-two years, so no movement of it can ever reach
this book. Restoration under 17 U.S.C. 104A cannot reach it either: a restored
copyright runs at most 95 years from publication, which for 1499 expired in 1594.

THE DATE WAS TESTED AGAINST THE BOOK'S OWN PAGES AND NOT TAKEN FROM THE
IDENTIFIER. The colophon on the last text leaf, n384 of 394, foliated `clxxviij`,
reads `Impressum Mediolani per magistrum Leonardum Pachel. Anno domini. M.cccc.
lxxxx viiij. die. xxvij. Augusti.` It was read in the page image, because this
text layer cannot render it. The volume carries no supplement, no second title
page and no second imprint; it ends at that colophon and then at flyleaves. See
the edition record. This test was run because two acquisitions had already been
refused for failing it -- the 1920 Missale Romanum and the Braga digitisation,
both caught by St Pius X, canonized 1954 -- and a 1499 book cannot carry a 1954
feast unless the scan is of a later state.

THE SCAN AND ITS TEXT LAYER ADD NOTHING FOR ANYONE TO OWN. A faithful mechanical
reproduction of a public-domain work is not original authorship (Bridgeman Art
Library v. Corel Corp., 36 F. Supp. 2d 191 (S.D.N.Y. 1999)), and machine optical
character recognition adds no human authorship on top of it. This text layer was
produced autonomously: the item records no `ocr` engine field, only
`ocr_converted = abbyy-to-hocr 1.1.37` and `ocr_module_version = 0.0.21`, so the
recognition was ABBYY's at an unstated version and there is no author to hold a
right in it. Note the limit of that argument, stated at length on the Braga
record: BRIDGEMAN FREES A SCAN OF PUBLIC-DOMAIN MATTER AND SAYS NOTHING ABOUT A
SCAN OF ANYTHING ELSE. Here there is nothing else, because every leaf of this
file is a photograph of a page printed in 1499.

THE HOST IS NOT THE SAME SHAPE OF HOST AS A BARE INTERNET ARCHIVE UPLOAD, AND
THE DIFFERENCE IS RECORDED RATHER THAN RELIED ON. The commissioning brief
described this as a Bibliotheque Sainte-Genevieve item rather than an Internet
Archive one. THAT IS NOT QUITE RIGHT AND THE CORRECTION MATTERS: it is an
Internet Archive item, `OEXV698`, in the collections `bibliothequesaintegenevieve`
and `bibliothequesaintegenevievelivres`, uploaded to the Internet Archive BY the
library from the address `bsg.numerisation@sorbonne-nouvelle.fr`. So there are
two statements to keep apart. The item's own metadata carries `rights = "domaine
public"` and `licenseurl = "http://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/"`,
and the source field names `Bibliotheque Sainte-Genevieve, OEXV 698 RES`. The
library's practice, distributing its digitised incunabula on the Internet Archive
under the Public Domain Mark since 2010, is consistent with both. NONE OF THAT IS
A LINK IN THIS BASIS. A digitising library's own terms are the library's
statement about its scans and cannot enlarge or shrink the copyright status of a
book printed in 1499; where a library asserts terms over a faithful reproduction
of public-domain matter, this repository's position is the Bridgeman one above.
The rights record states the position for all three hosts met in this lane:
src/sources/inventories/ambrosian-and-mozarabic-rights-v1.toml.

NOT RELIED ON, EXPRESSLY: that the Internet Archive item is available, that the
download succeeded, or that the host marks it public domain.
guidance/sources.md:395-400 holds availability and successful download
insufficient for `tracked`, and the Public Domain Mark was the whole of the prior
lt-hist corpus's ground for its books -- the ground refused at
src/sources/inventories/lt-hist-rights-audit-v1.toml. The mark is recorded as a
fact about the item and this basis would be unchanged if the item carried no mark
or a contradictory one.

edition.authority: None. This is a printer's book and no promulgating instrument is printed in it or claimed for it. The volume ends in its own colophon and nothing else: no bull, no decree, no episcopal letter.
edition.publication: Missale Ambrosianum. Milan: Leonhardus Pachel, 27 VIII 1499. Folio, illustrated. The copy digitised is Bibliotheque Sainte-Genevieve, shelfmark OEXV 698 RES, wanting leaves [*]1 and m8. Internet Archive item OEXV698, uploaded by the Bibliotheque Sainte-Genevieve itself.

alternate_titles: Missale iuxta ritum sanctae ecclesiae Mediolanensis
work.author: Archdiocese of Milan
work.description: The altar book of the Ambrosian rite -- the Latin use of the church of Milan, the largest non-Roman Latin rite still celebrated, and one of the uses left standing by the exempting clause of Quo primum. It is a Missal in the ordinary sense and it is NOT the Missale Romanum: it carries its own kalendar with its own Milanese archbishop-saints, its own Ordo Missae and Canon, a temporal cycle that begins six Sundays before Christmas, its own Holy Week and Easter Vigil, Commons, votive and Requiem Masses, blessings and Mass tones. IT MUST NOT BE FILED WITH THE ROMAN BOOK. work.catholic-church.missale-romanum is the Roman Rite's book; this is a different rite's, and the edge that does not exist between them is the point -- src/sources/inventories/latin-missal-acts-v1.toml records at its own line note that drawing one from the Roman line into the Ambrosian would assert a derivation in exactly the direction history runs the other way. It is registered under the archdiocese, on the pattern of work.archdiocese-of-braga.missale-bracarense, because the rite is the church of Milan's and the authority over the book has been the archbishop's throughout its printed tradition. The three editions registered here are printings, not promulgations: none of them carries a papal instrument, and what the 1640 and 1712 carry instead is an archbishop's own letter to his clergy.
work.title: Missale Ambrosianum
